attachments.origin_landmark: zygomatic bone, posterior to the zygomaticotemporal suture

actions: elevates the corner of the mouth (smiling)

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: The prime mover of a genuine (Duchenne) smile.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: High-frequency linear probe over the malar cheek, perpendicular to a horizontal line drawn laterally from the lateral canthus (the lateral canthus horizontal plane, LCHP); scanned at the perpendicular plane through the lateral canthus, orbital rim, midpoint of the frontal process of the zygomatic bone, or jugale point.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: The bony-origin fibers of zygomaticus major lie deep to the inferolateral orbicularis oculi: their superior margin sits 17.9-22.8 mm below the LCHP (varying by reference plane) and a further 3.0-4.5 mm deep to the orbicularis oculi's own inferior margin, which itself lies 4.7-5.5 mm below the skin.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: Ask the patient to smile broadly; the muscle bulges obliquely from the zygomatic arch toward the modiolus. On ultrasound its bony origin is seen as a distinct deep layer immediately beneath orbicularis oculi at the reference planes above.
structures_at_risk: orbicularis oculi, immediately superficial -- a shared BoNT field between the two muscles (e.g. for crow's feet) risks weakening ZMj and impairing the smile if injected too deep or too low
zygomaticus minor, running parallel and medial to ZMj toward the upper lip
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: Fibers of orbicularis oculi join the zygomaticus complex in a variable proportion of individuals (reported anywhere from ~23% to 100% depending on population studied), so ultrasound depth measurements should be treated as a guide rather than a fixed cutoff when avoiding the zygomaticus complex during orbicularis oculi injections.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Piao JZ, Lee JH, Hu KS, Kim HJ, Clin Anat 39(6):662-671 (2025), doi:10.1002/ca.24290 (https://doi.org/10.1002/ca.24290) -- retrieved via PubMed

trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: Upward beside the nose to the mid-forehead and nasal bridge.
trigger_points.activation_perpetuating_factors: Prolonged smiling or grimacing, dental procedures; satellite of sternocleidomastoid trigger-point activity.
trigger_points.source: Simons, Travell & Simons Trigger Point Manual -- as cited in this atlas's uploaded head and neck muscle reference document (Simons DG, Travell JG, Simons LS, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction: The Trigger Point Manual, Vol 1, 2nd ed., Williams & Wilkins, 1999)
